choices.content: Since \(\angle 1\) and \(\angle 2\) are supplementary, and \(\angle 2\) and \(\angle 3\) are supplementary, \(\angle 1=\angle 3\).
Since \(\angle 1\) and \(\angle 2\) are complementary, \(\angle 3\) and \(\angle 4\) are supplementary, and \(\angle 2=\angle 4\), \(\angle 1=\angle 3\).

question.prompt: Which of the following arguments is correct?

solutions.explanation: Both \(\angle 1\) and \(\angle 3\) are supplements of \(\angle 2\). Since supplements of the same angle are equal, \(\angle 1=\angle 3\). In the other choices, the sums of the angles differ or there is no common angle (or equal angles), so the conclusion cannot be drawn.
solutions.title: Check the common-angle condition
